newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH LEADING AUSTRALIA TOWARDS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH LEADING AUSTRALIA TOWARDS VICTORY.

text.p: Mark Waugh was steering Australia towards victory over South Africa on the fourth day of the second test on Monday with an unbeaten 86.
Needing 270 to win and take a 2-0 winning lead in the three-test series, Australia extended the overnight 145 for three to 204 for five at lunch.
Twins Mark and Steve Waugh weathered a potentially lethal first spell from fast bowler Allan Donald to carry their fourth wicket stand to 54 without undue alarm.
But Steve Waugh (18) then drove a wide, swinging half volley from occasional seamer Jacques Kallis into the covers where Hansie Cronje dived at full stretch to his left to take a fine catch.

Both Mark Waugh and Greg Blewett were beaten by numerous deliveries from left-arm wrist spinner Paul Adams that turned and bounced but, in between survival, Mark never failed to attack the loose ball.
Fifteen minutes before lunch Adams finally took the wicket that had appeared so inevitable when he yorked Blewett for seven to make Australia 192 for five.
But Mark Waugh showed the steely resiliance so often associated with his brother throughout the morning, taking Australia to within 66 of victory at the interval, with Michael Bevan four not out.
